title: The Evening Brief: Cutdown chaos, arrests, and tennis upsets close Monday's slate
dek: NFL rosters locked in after Sunday's 6 p.m. deadline with trades and two open disciplinary cases, while Djokovic's first-round US Open exit and Scheffler's earnings milestone rounded out a day that moved the needle across three sports.
author: GoCheckMySports
key_fact: Monday brought roster finality to the NFL, unresolved legal questions for two teams, a Grand Slam upset that reshapes the US Open draw, and a golf earnings record that caps a dominant summer for Scheffler.
bottom_line: Monday's NFL cutdown day settled rosters into regular-season shape while leaving two disciplinary cases, Keenan Allen's DWI arrest and Josh Jacobs' exempt-list placement, unresolved ahead of Week 1. Djokovic's first-round US Open exit reshaped the men's draw at a Grand Slam already missing Sinner; Alcaraz's comeback and Sabalenka's three-peat pursuit will test whether either can sustain their form. Scheffler closed the earnings gap on Woods with his Tour Championship victory. Watch the Colts' and Packers' legal timelines, Ohtani's next pitching date, Jacobs' three-day appeal window, and whether Alcaraz and leading women's contenders advance from the early US Open rounds.
body: The NFL's 53-man roster deadline on Sunday produced the ordinary churn of cutdown day alongside two significant off-field matters that remain open. The Bears traded 2023 second-round pick Gervon Dexter, a 6-foot-6, 326-pound defensive tackle who started all 19 games last season, to the Falcons for cornerback Clark Phillips and a fifth-round pick. Buffalo sent center Sedrick Van Pran-Granger, a 2024 fifth-round pick who appeared in 31 regular-season games for the Bills, to Indianapolis in exchange for a 2027 sixth-round pick (the Bills sent back a seventh-rounder). The Giants' initial 53-man roster included Odell Beckham Jr., 33, after the receiver sat out all of 2025. Aaron Donald ended his retirement and signed a one-year deal with the Rams worth $20 million plus $10 million in incentives, reuniting with a roster that includes reigning MVP Matthew Stafford and newly acquired Myles Garrett.

Two arrests complicate the picture ahead of Week 1. Keenan Allen, 34, was arrested early Sunday on preliminary charges of DWI and DWI endangering a person, both misdemeanors, with a blood alcohol content of 0.08 or more, according to the Indianapolis Metro Police Department. The arrest occurred hours after Allen caught one pass for 24 yards in the Colts' preseason game against Detroit on Saturday; he signed with Indianapolis less than two weeks earlier on a contract that could be worth up to $8.32 million. The honest read is that the reporting establishes what authorities charged but does not yet show what the Colts or the NFL will decide. The Green Bay Packers' Josh Jacobs was placed on the commissioner's exempt list on Sunday, rendering him ineligible to play, practice, or attend games while facing misdemeanor charges of battery and criminal damage to property announced August 28. Jacobs, a three-time Pro Bowl selection, will be paid his salary while the league reviews the case; he and the NFLPA have three days from formal notification to appeal.

In tennis, Novak Djokovic, ranked No. 5 and seeded fourth at the US Open, lost to Mariano Navone, ranked No. 49, in a first-round marathon on August 31. The 24-time Grand Slam champion displayed visible distress, vomiting several times and using an inhaler during breaks; he attributed the loss to health issues that have plagued him throughout 2026. The defeat marked his first first-round exit at Flushing Meadows and his first opening-round Grand Slam loss since 2006. Aryna Sabalenka opened her three-peat bid with a 6-2, 6-4 victory over Camila Osorio, while Venus Williams, 46, lost to Sofia Kenin the same day, extending her singles losing streak to 15 consecutive matches since her return last July. World No. 1 Jannik Sinner remains absent through injury; defending champion Carlos Alcaraz is making his comeback from a long-term wrist injury. The draw is now shaped by whether Alcaraz can progress and whether Sabalenka, whose ranking lead has shrunk significantly since April, can sustain her form through the tournament.

Scheffler's 16-under victory at the Tour Championship on Sunday broke Tiger Woods' 25-year-old PGA Tour career earnings record. Scheffler's career total now stands at $130.39 million, surpassing Woods' $120.9 million mark. The Tour Championship victory earned Scheffler a $10 million winner's purse and his second FedEx Cup title. In baseball, Max Scherzer struck out 10 batters against the Mariners on August 30, moving into ninth place on baseball's all-time strikeouts list with 3,535 career strikeouts, surpassing Gaylord Perry. The Cubs' Pete Crow-Armstrong hit three home runs in a 17-5 victory over the Reds on August 29, sustaining his candidacy in a two-man National League MVP race against Shohei Ohtani, who has won four MVP awards in the past five seasons. The Red Sox activated outfielder Roman Anthony and shortstop Trevor Story from the injured list on Sunday after each missed more than three months, addressing depth ahead of the September stretch. Shohei Ohtani will not pitch Sunday, with Dodgers manager Dave Roberts stating Ohtani is "not 100%" and his return timeline remains uncertain, though the team still expects his return as a pitcher this season. The Cardinals placed rookie JJ Wetherholt, a National League Rookie of the Year candidate, on the injured list before Sunday's series finale against the Pirates with right wrist tendinitis after he played through discomfort for weeks.
